source_text_reference: Saravali 19.8 Sanskrit prayo (normally/often); conjoined 5 or 6 classical planets, source conjunction threshold unresolved
time_grid: UTC midnight every five days starting 1800-01-01 to exclusive 2200-01-01
source_code_approach: For each 5-day sample JD, use swe.calc_ut(jd, body, swe.FLG_MOSEPH | (swe.FLG_SIDEREAL for sidereal mode)), set swe.set_sid_mode(mode), take int(ecliptic_longitude//30), count largest 30° sign group across Sun/Moon/Mars/Mercury/Jupiter/Venus/Saturn.
interpretation: Results are sensitive to the choice of sidereal/tropical zodiac grid (not simply source-independent fixed trait prevalence).
Zero all-seven observations on this sparse five-day grid does NOT contradict known two-day all-seven episodes (1821 Apr02–03 and 1962 Feb04–05); the grid missed them.
The FULL every-day 400y Lahiri scan counts 4 seven-body day snapshots and is documented in SARAVALI_CONJUNCTION_SKY_SUPPORT_B30.json. DO NOT replace that with these sparse counts.
Even a daily sign group is not a degree-orb conjunction, nor does it imply same house under non-whole-sign house systems.
Selection of ayanamsa in an eventual human model must be fixed before interpreting outcomes; source/orb/strength may change rates further.

provenance.source_code: Standalone local 5-day-grid script executed successfully against mounted pyswisseph; this JSON specifies its exact arithmetic loop. No user birth data, participant answers or human predictions.
provenance.external_corroboration: https://vedicmystics.com/2020/04/18/all-grahas-in-one-sign/ — non-primary community site independently reports the 1821 and 1962 examples, but does NOT validate predictive astrology.
